why_it_is_authored: A region has no honest derivation. Every candidate available from a chunk's own fields is the id prefix, and a region name contained in an id prefix names a slug rather than a place. So this one is written down by a person, like every other region on the map, and the code is only allowed to apply it — never to invent one beside it.
why_it_passes_the_check: An id prefix is a single token: the split that produces it breaks on space. A region name containing a space therefore cannot be a substring of any prefix, whatever the ids turn out to be. That is why this name is safe structurally rather than by luck, and why replacing it with a single word would be unsafe even if today's ids happened to allow it.
note: Owned by neither language. Both declare their own constant and both assert it against this file, so changing the name on one side alone turns the other side's suite red.
